doc.title: Ray Blue interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 23, 2022

title: Doc Vollmer and the band today
summary: Blue praises Doc Vollmer's mission to keep older musicians in the public eye, and lists current gigs and personnel.

venues.name: Cross Cultural Connection Saturday night series

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Well Doc, you know Doc was part of the show as well because Doc made a point of informing the audience of the history and the importance of the development of the band and this sound and this music. You know? He made — his opening remarks were very powerful and very much needed. And the way he pulled people together, and the way he cared about people. Doc cares about people. You know? Doc would make sure cats had — he would make sure there were gigs because he said these musicians who made all this great music, they’re not appreciated anymore. I have to find a way to keep them in the public eye because that’s where they deserve to be, and that’s how he created the band and he kept it going. Forty-some years. Actually — excuse me — he called on me to kind of help out with some bookings when we can, and we’re going to be playing on the second of July in Peekskill as part of the Cross Cultural Connection Saturday night series. So we’re going to be doing that, we’re going to be at the New Rochelle Library in December, we booked that one. We were down in the Rocky Mountains, for the Monk Festival last year, we went down to North Carolina, we went down there. Yeah. Now that Zeke isn’t with us anymore, Danny Mixon plays piano with us now, yeah. We also, oh yeah there were a couple of other trombone players too, Ron Wilkins, a phenomenal trombone player. Clarence Banks, he went down to Carolina with us. He’s with the Basie band and he played with us as well. Yeah, it’s been really nice. So we’re keeping things going, Doc’s keeping things going.
